question.text: Mr. Sharma, a resident Indian, wants to invest Rs. 30,000 in a mutual fund scheme of ABC Mutual Fund. He does not have a PAN card. He has already invested Rs. 25,000 across other schemes of the same fund house in the last 8 months. Which statement is correct regarding PAN exemption for micro investments?

answer.text: He is NOT eligible for PAN exemption as his aggregate investment under all schemes of the fund house would exceed Rs. 50,000, reckoned on a rolling 12-month period or in a financial year
He is eligible for PAN exemption since each individual investment is below Rs. 50,000
He is eligible for PAN exemption as the Rs. 50,000 limit applies per scheme, not per fund house
He is NOT eligible because PAN exemption is only available for SIP investments, not lump sum

explanation.text: The Logic: The PAN exemption for micro investments applies only when the aggregate investment under all schemes of a fund house is up to Rs. 50,000, reckoned on a rolling 12-month period or in a financial year. Mr. Sharma's aggregate would be Rs. 25,000 + Rs. 30,000 = Rs. 55,000, which exceeds the Rs. 50,000 threshold under either measurement period, so the exemption does not apply. The Trap: The Rs. 50,000 limit is aggregate across all schemes of the fund house, not per scheme, and the mode of investment (lump sum or SIP) does not change the threshold. Note: The measurement period is a rolling 12-month period or a financial year, as stated in the source.
